estimated_study_time.text: Plan about 2 hours for this lesson, with time for reading-skill review, prompt analysis, unfamiliar-word strategies, practice items, and self-checking.

chapter_summary.text: This lesson focuses on reading skills such as main idea or gist, writer’s purpose, organization, inference, explicit and implicit information, classifying and categorizing information, and inferring unfamiliar words. It provides further skills practice for Reading: Multiple-choice, choose single answer and Reading: Multiple-choice, choose multiple answers.

evidence_spans.quote:

• Main idea or gist: Read for and identify the main idea or theme of the text

• Writer’s purpose: Read for and understand the function of what the writer says or identify the reasons why 
the writer mentions specific pieces of information

• Organization: Read for and identify the overall organization and connections between pieces of information
• Inference: Read a text and infer meanings, form generalizations, make predictions, find relationships or draw 
conclusions

• Comprehending explicit and implicit information 
• Classifying and categorizing information
• Inferring the meaning of unfamiliar words

core_lessons.title: Infer Meaning From Overall Meaning And Writer’s Opinion

explanation.text: Prompts that ask test takers to infer meaning require careful reading of the passage and options, with attention to overall meaning and the writer’s opinion.

core_lessons.title: For Some Inference Prompts, Read The Passage First

explanation.text: For the prompt “Which of the following can be inferred from the text?”, it is better to read the passage first to prevent becoming confused by the options.

first to prevent becoming confused by the options.

explanation.text: Read the options carefully, paraphrase each one to check meaning, eliminate options that seem obviously incorrect, make a first guess, and re-read the passage to double-check each option.

question.text: A prompt says, “Which of the following can be inferred from the text?” What should you do before choosing an option?

answer.text: Read the passage first, identify its gist and overall meaning, then read and check the options carefully.

question.text: You see the sentence “It was ubiquitous, with every category of crime falling in every part of the country.” Which context phrase helps you infer the meaning of “ubiquitous”?

answer.text: The phrase “every part of the country” helps you infer that “ubiquitous” is connected with being everywhere or wide-ranging.

question.text: A question asks for words that mean “residences” in the passage. What should you pay attention to in the prompt and passage?

answer.text: Pay attention to “in the passage,” underline possible matching words, and use context to check whether each one has the same meaning as “residences.”

question.text: Why should you paraphrase each multiple-choice option before eliminating it?

answer.text: Paraphrasing helps you make sure you understand the meaning of each option before deciding whether it is obviously incorrect or needs to be checked against the passage.

review_checklist.text: I can identify whether a prompt asks for gist, inference, writer’s purpose, or a specific word meaning.
I can read a passage for overall meaning before answering an inference prompt.
I can paraphrase answer options before eliminating or selecting them.
I can use context clues and word parts to infer the meaning of unfamiliar words.
I can notice when a word’s meaning depends on how it is used in the passage.
I can reflect on which multiple-choice strategies helped me answer efficiently and accurately.
